name: Supererogation
overview: The doctrine of supererogation, which teaches the idea of excessive and meritorious righteousness beyond God's commands, is challenged by Scripture. Ezekiel 33:12-13 reveals that a person's own righteousness cannot save them on the day of their transgression, emphasizing that trusting in personal merit leads to death rather than life. Furthermore, Luke 17:10 underscores the believer's humble recognition that fulfilling God's commands is simply their duty, not grounds for boasting or claiming extra merit. Together, these verses affirm that righteousness is not a matter of accumulating excess works but of faithful obedience grounded in dependence on God.
